claim.quote: With an exposure of 0.233g $\times$ 12 hours, we place the most stringent constraints on dark matter masses between 44 and 87 MeV/$c^2$, with the lowest unexplored cross section of 4 $\times 10^{-32}$ cm$^2$ at 87 MeV/$c^2$.

key_value.note: Lowest unexplored cross section, at 87 MeV/c^2, spin-independent DM-nucleon; 90% CL limit per the paper.

name: First Limits on Light Dark Matter Interactions in a Low Threshold Two Channel Athermal Phonon Detector from the TESSERACT Collaboration
notes: Attached to experiment:spice as well: the TAUP 2025 slides list this limit under SPICE ('Dark Matter limit published: arXiv:2503.03683v2'); the paper itself says only 'TESSERACT Collaboration'.
The abstract prints the resolution as '361.5 +- 0.4 MeV/c^2' (a unit slip in the abstract; the paper's resolution is a few hundred meV), so it is not used as a number here.

summary.plain: A tiny silicon chip run above ground at Berkeley for 12 hours searched for dark matter heavier than 44 MeV and lighter than 87 MeV. It saw no dark matter and set the tightest limits yet in that mass range.
summary.technical: Spin-independent dark matter-nucleon limit from a 1 cm^2 x 1 mm (0.233 g) silicon athermal-phonon detector with two-channel rejection of sensor-coupled low-energy backgrounds, operated above ground at UC Berkeley; exposure 0.233 g x 12 hours; a conservative salting technique reaches the lowest mass probed. A prototype of the TESSERACT programme (a SPICE-type detector per the TAUP 2025 slides), not the Modane setup.

title: First Limits on Light Dark Matter Interactions in a Low Threshold Two Channel Athermal Phonon Detector from the TESSERACT Collaboration
why_it_matters: The abstract states that the result reaches the lowest dark matter mass ever probed via a direct detection experiment, using a detector small enough to be scaled into the TESSERACT payload.
